definition: Calais is a service created by Thomson Reuters that automatically extracts semantic information from web pages in a format that can be used on the semantic web.
details: Calais was launched in January 2008, and is free to use. The technology is now available via the website of Refinitiv, a provider of financial market data and infrastructure founded in 2018, that is a subsidiary of London Stock Exchange Group. The Calais Web service reads unstructured text and returns Resource Description Framework formatted results identifying entities, facts and events within the text. The service appears to be based on technology acquired when Reuters purchased ClearForest in 2007. The technology has also been used to automatically tag blog articles, and organize museum collections. Calais uses natural language processing technologies delivered via a web service interface.

explainer.lead: Calais is a Thomson Reuters service that turns unstructured text into machine-readable descriptions of the entities, facts, and events it contains. Launched in January 2008 and free to use, it helps computers make practical use of text that was originally written for people.

tiers.eli5: Calais is like a helper that reads a story and makes labels for the people, places, and happenings in it. Instead of leaving the story as one big block of words, it returns organized notes that a computer can understand. This makes the information easier to sort and connect.
tiers.practitioner: Send unstructured text to the Calais web service and consume its Resource Description Framework output describing identified entities, facts, and events. It can support automated tagging and collection organization; downstream systems must be designed to handle RDF rather than expecting plain keyword labels.
tiers.paperLevel: Calais can be described as a web-service mapping f(text) -> RDF statements, where the statements identify entities, facts, and events in unstructured text using natural language processing. It is a semantic extraction service rather than a specified algorithm or evaluation benchmark. The description does not establish extraction accuracy or performance limits.

explainer.example: For a blog article describing a person, an organization, and an event, Calais can return RDF results identifying those items. A publishing system can then use the results to tag the article automatically.

explainer.intuition: Written text contains useful names, relationships, and happenings, but computers cannot easily organize them while they remain buried in prose. Calais reads that prose and expresses selected information as structured semantic data.
howItWorks: Provide unstructured text, such as text from a web page.
The web service processes the text with natural language processing technologies.
It identifies entities, facts, and events within the text.
It returns the extracted information as Resource Description Framework formatted results.
explainer.whyItMatters: Calais bridges human-readable text and semantic-web data, making information easier to tag, organize, and connect without relying entirely on manual annotation. Its technology was also used beyond web-page extraction, including blog tagging and museum collection organization.
misconceptions: Calais is not simply a keyword list generator; its output identifies entities, facts, and events in RDF.
It does not require text to be structured first; its input is unstructured text.
Although created by Thomson Reuters, the technology is now available through Refinitiv's website.
